spec.alternative_hypothesis: The lagged BAA10Y change (basis points, latest available at the decision close) has a positive coefficient in the daily BAA10Y->VIX partial lead-lag regression (spread widening predicts higher next-day VIX log changes), with partial R-squared at least 0.005 and a positive holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared. Note on wording: the planner draft's 'positive, out-of-sample component' refers to positive incremental explanatory power (incremental R-squared above zero), not to a positive coefficient — the expected coefficient sign is positive on the economic argument in the mechanism, independently of that wording.
spec.benchmark: Own-history baseline: next-day VIX log change predicted from its own lagged log change and the SPX common-factor control only, without the lagged BAA10Y change
cost_assumptions: VIX is a volatility index and is not tradable; VIX exposure requires VIX futures (CFE), and futures roll costs cannot be measured from free data: Yahoo VX=F returns no data (verified by study 003 on 2026-11-18, re-verified here on 2026-11-19 — HTTP 404) and no other reliable free VIX futures series was found
The cost gate is therefore informational, not a verdict criterion; the holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared carries the economic weight
The reported gross sign-rule edge applies no costs at all and is an upper bound on any tradable edge
spec.cost_model: Informational only (study 003's precedent for a volatility-index target): VIX is not tradable; VIX exposure requires VIX futures, and futures roll costs cannot be measured from free data (Yahoo VX=F returns no data — verified by study 003 on 2026-11-18 and re-verified on 2026-11-19, HTTP 404 — and no other reliable free VIX futures series was found). The trial reports the gross sign-rule edge on holdout out-of-sample augmented forecasts (1x, always invested while positioned, no costs applied) as an informational upper bound on any tradable edge, with a block-bootstrap confidence interval; the holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared carries the economic weight. The cost gate is not a verdict criterion.
exclusions: Bars outside the sample window (2003-01-02 to 2026-11-19) are out of sample; the panel ends where the data ends (the FRED legs bind, one trading day behind the fetch date).
Incomplete synchronized rows are excluded and counted.
FRED empty-field missing values are excluded at fetch time and counted.
The first two panel return rows have no lagged BAA10Y change and are dropped.
The naive unlagged alignment, the no-factor control, the reverse placebo and the sub-period stability split are descriptive only and are not in the test family.
known_confounders: BAA10Y is defined as the BAA yield minus the 10-year Treasury yield (DGS10); the spread change nets out the rates level by construction, so a common rates shock moves both legs and is differenced out — the predictor measures the credit-specific component. The DGS10 leg is therefore not a separate control.

VIX is itself an equity-volatility measure, so the equity channel is partly the mechanism under test rather than a confounder to control: an equity shock that moves both the spread and equity volatility is the transmission the hypothesis describes, not a bias to remove. The SPX control absorbs the day-t equity move itself, not the volatility channel.

The 2-trading-day BAA10Y availability lag is verified behaviorally (6b evidence probe 2026-11-18T21:45Z plus the fetch-time re-check) and assumed constant across the sample. If the historical posting lag differed, the predictor alignment is wrong for those periods.
FRED series are revised over time; the fetch records the current vintage. Historical values as first published may differ from the current vintage (revision risk is unmodelled).

The own-history baseline uses the VIX log change over day t as a predictor for the change over t+1. Under the study's source-based PIT convention (FRED posts day-t values the next business day), the day-t VIX value is published the next morning, so the baseline uses information the FRED source had not yet published at the decision close. The same convention was used in studies 003 and 009. It strengthens the baseline against the source, so the incremental test is conservative: the source must beat a baseline that already knows the target's most recent change.

The SPX control is the log change over day t (SPX[t], study 003's factor-alignment precedent): Yahoo posts the close the same evening, so it is knowable at the decision close. It absorbs the day-t common equity shock by design — that is what a same-day control is for.
The sample covers the 2008 crisis, the 2020 COVID crash and the 2022 rate shock; transmission may be regime-dependent. Sub-period stability is descriptive only.

VIX log changes are close to unpredictable (study 003's base-model R-squared for next-day VIX log changes was about 0.012); the baseline explains little, so the incremental R-squared is measured against a weak baseline.

The PIT store records available_at equal to the event time (adapter limitation); the publication lag is enforced in the trial's panel construction via the study-007 lagged-changes module, not in the stored observations.
spec.mechanism: A widening BAA credit spread reflects rising credit risk premia and tightening financial conditions: corporate funding costs rise relative to Treasuries as default risk is repriced. Stress in credit markets typically coincides with rising equity volatility, as the same risk-off impulse drives deleveraging and flight-to-quality flows, and as falling equity prices mechanically raise leverage and hence volatility (the leverage effect). The spread is an end-of-day published signal, so any transmission should appear the next trading day. The expected sign is positive: spread widening predicts higher next-day VIX log changes.
spec.missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count. FRED empty-field missing values are excluded at fetch time and counted.
model_definition: Partial lead-lag OLS with Newey-West HAC standard errors (daily lagged BAA10Y change -> next-day VIX log change)
Purged walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation of the primary model (baseline: own history plus SPX control; augmented: plus lagged BAA10Y change)
Naive lead-lag scan (lags 0-5, raw Pearson correlations) as a descriptive upper bound (not in the test family)
Descriptive only: unlagged (naive) alignment, no-factor upper-bound control, reverse placebo (VIX->BAA10Y), sub-period stability

Cost gate is informational only (study 003's precedent): the gross sign-rule edge on holdout out-of-sample augmented forecasts, no costs applied, with a block-bootstrap confidence interval — not a verdict criterion
spec.multiple_testing_family: Credit-spread transmission to equity volatility (1 test: daily lagged BAA10Y change -> next-day VIX log change)
spec.null_hypothesis: Lagged BAA10Y changes have no incremental predictive value for next-day VIX log changes over VIX's own history and the SPX common-factor control, with dependence controls.
spec.primary_metric: Partial R-squared of the lagged BAA10Y change (bp, latest available at the decision close) in the daily BAA10Y->VIX partial lead-lag regression
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted primary p-value at or above 0.05
Holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared at or below 0
spec.research_question: Does the most recent BAA10Y credit-spread change available at the close predict the next-day VIX log change beyond VIX's own history and the SPX common-factor control?
spec.target_definition: Next-day VIX log change (FRED VIXCLS, CBOE Volatility Index); the predictor is the most recent BAA10Y level change in basis points available at the decision close — under the verified 2-trading-day BAA10Y posting lag, the change ending two trading days before the decision close.
spec.title: Credit-spread changes lead equity volatility (VIX)
